title: CFNIS Command Chain — Trudeau & LeBlanc Dossier

bgen_simon_trudeau.name: Major-General Simon Trudeau (later BGen)
bgen_simon_trudeau.role: Canadian Forces Provost Marshal — commands ALL military police

obstruction_finding.finding: MPCC watchdog accused Provost Marshal of obstructing independent reviews of complaints
obstruction_finding.details: Subjected documents to excessive redaction, preventing MPCC from having full disclosure of evidence
obstruction_finding.pattern: Only provided partial materials when requested by oversight agency
obstruction_finding.his_response: Statement claiming to fully support MPCC mandate — while actively obstructing it

civilian_oversight_resistance.finding: Military police STILL resisting civilian oversight as of 2025
civilian_oversight_resistance.pattern: Annual MPCC reports repeatedly document same resistance pattern

provost_marshal_report.note: His own annual report — compare claims vs MPCC findings

misconduct_statement.note: Statement addressing misconduct allegations against MP members

lcol_eric_leblanc.name: Lieutenant-Colonel Eric LeBlanc
lcol_eric_leblanc.role: CFNIS Commander — operational command of all sensitive investigations

vance_investigation.finding: CFNIS recommended ENDING the investigation into Gen. Jonathan Vance within HOURS of his swearing-in as Chief of Defence Staff in 2015
vance_investigation.significance: Vance later faced sexual misconduct charges — the investigation LeBlanc closed could have prevented years of abuse
vance_investigation.pattern: The investigative body that is supposed to hold senior leadership accountable recommended closing the case on the day the subject gained maximum power

independence_claim.his_statement: Only the provost marshal can direct me to conduct an investigation — nobody else
independence_claim.reality: This means investigations into senior leaders require approval from a chain that reports to those same leaders

committee_testimony.topic: CFNIS handling of sexual misconduct cases

pattern: The Provost Marshal (Trudeau) commands all military police and obstructed civilian oversight. The CFNIS Commander (LeBlanc) reports to the Provost Marshal and recommended closing the Vance investigation on Day 1. This is not a bug — it is a self-protecting chain of command where the investigative body answers to the institution it is supposed to investigate.
